title: Two broad ASASSN-14ko flares follow one UV count-rate relation across the predicted dip phase
abstract: We test whether the broad UV rises of ASASSN-14ko cycles 28 and 29 need a new spectral component at the X-ray clock phase. We use 68 paired Swift UVW2 and UVM2 aperture count rates from a signed campaign publication. A straight relation explains 99.4 and 99.1 percent of measured variance. A common slope with separate constant intercepts explains 99.23 percent in both cycles. We find no clear change at the predicted dip phase. A three-day block bootstrap limits slope changes to about ten percent, but seven-day blocks permit a 38 percent increase in cycle 28. This gives a spectral constraint on broad-flare models. It does not identify the period-stall mechanism. Two bands cannot separate components with similar colours. The source photometry lacks full sensitivity corrections, and the dip phase is predicted in these X-ray off-state cycles.
